Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

initiative noun

acting first, without being asked

also on my own initiative, take the initiative, unasked, unprompted, without being asked, show initiative, unprovoked

classical

Ter. Eun. 813: ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō
Publil. Sent. B 1: ultrō sī offerās
Traupman 400

ultrō

adverb

unasked, of one’s own accord; making the first move

Lewis & Short draws the line: ultrō faciō, nōn rogātus; sponte faciō, nōn coāctus neque adjūtus. So ultrō is acting unasked, and goes with offering, coming forward, starting a fight. Its literal sense is “beyond, to the far side” (ultrō citrōque, to and fro).

Other words

  • meā (tuā, suā) sponte — on my (your, his) own initiative; unforced

    phrase: ablative of the defective noun spōns with the possessive · also used · classical · Traupman 101: meā sponte; Liv. 1.39.2: suā sponte experrēctus; Traupman 101; Traupman 333

    Without compulsion or help, by one’s own will, or of a thing, by itself (see own).

Examples

  • Bis est grātum quod opus est, ultrō sī offerās.

    what is needed is twice welcome if you offer it unaskedPublil. Sent. B 1

  • nē exspectēmus quidem, dum rogēmur; studium semper adsit, cūnctātiō absit

    let us not even wait to be asked; let there always be eagerness and never hesitationCic. Amic. 44

  • Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.

    when you want it, they don’t; when you don’t, they want it of their own accordTer. Eun. 813

  • movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset

    she forbade them to move the boy until he woke up of his own accordLiv. 1.39.2

  • Nēmō tē rogāvit, et tamen ultrō adjūvistī.

    Nobody asked you, and yet you helped of your own accord.composed

See also own, begin, offer.
